quests.instruction: A square has a dot on its top left corner. It makes a quarter turn clockwise. Where is the dot now?
quests.hint: Follow the dot a quarter of the way around, in the direction clock hands move.
quests.explanation: Turning clockwise carries the top left corner to the top right corner, so the dot ends up there.
quests.funFact: Following a marked corner is the easiest way to track what a turn has done to a shape.

quests.instruction: A square has a dot on its top left corner. It is flipped left to right, and then given a half turn. Where is the dot now?
quests.hint: Do the moves one at a time and follow the dot after each one.
quests.explanation: The flip sends the dot from the top left to the top right. The half turn then sends it to the opposite corner, the bottom left.
quests.funFact: Two moves in a row can give the same result as one different move.

quests.instruction: A rectangle is 8 cm wide and 3 cm tall, with a flag on its bottom right corner. It makes a quarter turn counterclockwise. What is true now?
quests.correctAnswer: It is 3 cm wide and 8 cm tall, with the flag at the top right
options: It is 8 cm wide and 3 cm tall, with the flag at the top right
It is 3 cm wide and 8 cm tall, with the flag at the top right
It is 3 cm wide and 8 cm tall, with the flag at the bottom left
quests.hint: A quarter turn swaps wide and tall. Then follow the flag against the direction of clock hands.
quests.explanation: A quarter turn swaps the width and the height. Turning counterclockwise carries the bottom right corner up to the top right.
quests.funFact: Surveyors place flags at the corners of a plot of land to mark its edges.

quests.instruction: Which letter does not look the same when held up to a mirror on its right side?
quests.hint: Imagine the letter's right half swapping places with its left half.
quests.explanation: H and A are balanced, so their two halves match and the mirror image looks the same. R has a bump and a leg on one side only, so its mirror image looks different.
quests.funFact: Some ambulances print the word AMBULANCE backwards on the front so drivers can read it in their mirrors.

quests.instruction: A banner says WOW. It is given a half turn. What does it read now?
quests.hint: Turn each letter upside down, and remember that the order of the letters also reverses.
quests.explanation: Upside down, W looks like M and O looks like O. The half turn also reverses the order, so WOW reads MOM.
quests.funFact: The word NOON reads the same upside down because each of its letters looks unchanged.

quests.instruction: Which word looks the same in a mirror?
quests.hint: Check that each letter looks the same in a mirror, and that the word reads the same backward.
quests.explanation: T and O look the same in a mirror, and TOOT reads the same backward, so its mirror image is unchanged. D and B look different in a mirror.
quests.funFact: Words that read the same backward are called palindromes, like noon and level.

quests.instruction: A rectangle has two long sides and two short sides. After how many quarter turns does it first look exactly the same as at the start?
quests.hint: After one quarter turn, a wide rectangle becomes tall.
quests.explanation: One quarter turn changes the rectangle from wide to tall, so it looks different. After two quarter turns, which is a half turn, it looks the same again.
quests.funFact: The number of times a shape matches itself in one full turn is called its order of rotation.

quests.instruction: A triangle with three equal sides is turned until it looks the same as at the start, without going all the way around. How much of a full turn is that?
quests.correctAnswer: One third of a full turn
options: A quarter of a full turn
One third of a full turn
quests.hint: Each corner has to move into the next corner's place.
quests.explanation: Each corner moves into the next corner's place after one third of a full turn, so the triangle looks the same. A quarter turn or a half turn leaves a corner pointing the wrong way.
quests.funFact: A fan with three blades looks the same after a third of a turn.

quests.instruction: A shape looks the same after a quarter turn, a half turn, and a three-quarter turn. Which shape could it be?
quests.hint: It must look the same after every quarter turn, not just some of them.
quests.explanation: A square has four matching sides and corners, so it matches itself after every quarter turn. A long rectangle matches only after a half turn, and a triangle matches after none of them.
quests.funFact: A circle matches itself after any turn at all.

quests.instruction: A coin lies flat, then is tilted so that, from where you stand, it looks like an oval. What shape is the coin itself?
quests.hint: Tilting changes how a shape looks from where you stand, not what it is.
quests.explanation: The coin's edge does not change when it tilts. It only looks like an oval because of the angle you view it from, but the coin is still a circle.
quests.funFact: Artists learn to draw circles as ovals to show them from an angle.

quests.instruction: A rectangular door swings open, and from near the wall it looks narrower and narrower. What shape is the door itself?
quests.hint: Does the door itself bend or shrink when it swings?
quests.explanation: The door does not change as it swings. It only looks narrower from your position, and it is still a rectangle.
quests.funFact: Your brain keeps track of an object's real shape even when it looks different from different angles. This is called shape constancy.

quests.instruction: Standing between two straight railway rails, you see them seem to meet far away. Are the rails still parallel?
quests.correctAnswer: Yes, they only look like they meet
options: Yes, they only look like they meet
Only the nearer parts are parallel
quests.hint: Think about whether trains could run on rails that really met.
quests.explanation: Rails stay the same distance apart all along. Distant objects look smaller, so the gap seems to shrink, but the rails are parallel.
quests.funFact: Artists use this effect, called perspective, to make flat drawings look deep.

quests.instruction: A house shape is a square with a triangle on top. It is given a half turn. Which shape is on top now?
quests.hint: A half turn swaps top and bottom.
quests.explanation: Before the turn the triangle is on top. A half turn puts it at the bottom, so the square is now on top.
quests.funFact: Turning a drawing upside down can help you notice the shapes in it.

quests.instruction: An ice cream drawing has a triangle cone at the bottom and a circle scoop on top. It makes a quarter turn clockwise. Where is the scoop now?
quests.hint: Clockwise carries the top of a shape toward the right.
quests.explanation: A quarter turn clockwise sends the top to the right, so the scoop is on the right side and the cone points left.
quests.funFact: Seen from the side a cone looks like a triangle, and seen from above it looks like a circle.

quests.instruction: A row of shapes reads circle, square, triangle from left to right. The row is flipped left to right. What is the new order?
quests.hint: A left to right flip reverses the whole row.
quests.explanation: Flipping left to right swaps the two ends and keeps the middle, so the order becomes triangle, square, circle.
quests.funFact: A mirror reverses the order of anything laid out from left to right.

quests.instruction: A triangle has sides of 5 cm, 5 cm, and 8 cm. Which triangle is the same size and shape, just turned?
quests.correctAnswer: Sides of 5 cm, 8 cm, and 5 cm
options: Sides of 6 cm, 6 cm, and 8 cm
Sides of 5 cm, 5 cm, and 9 cm
Sides of 5 cm, 8 cm, and 5 cm
quests.hint: Turning changes the order you read the sides in, not their lengths.
quests.explanation: The triangle with sides 5, 8, and 5 has the same set of lengths, so it is the same triangle with the sides read in a different order. The other triangles have different side lengths.
quests.funFact: Three side lengths are enough to fix the exact shape of a triangle.

quests.instruction: A rectangle is 12 cm wide and 5 cm tall. It makes a quarter turn, and then another quarter turn the same way. How wide is it now?
quests.hint: Two quarter turns make a half turn. What does a half turn do to wide and tall?
quests.explanation: The first quarter turn makes it 5 cm wide and 12 cm tall. The second turns it back, so it is 12 cm wide again.
quests.funFact: Two quarter turns in the same direction always add up to a half turn.

quests.instruction: Eli traces a hexagon and cuts out a copy. The copy fits back into the outline after being turned one sixth of a full turn. What does this tell you about the hexagon?
quests.correctAnswer: All six sides and corners are equal
options: All six sides and corners are equal
quests.hint: Every corner has to move into the next corner's place.
quests.explanation: To fit back after a sixth of a turn, each side and corner must match the next one, so all six sides and corners are equal. This is a regular hexagon.
quests.funFact: Honeycomb cells repeat this pattern because each cell can be turned a sixth of a turn and still fit.

quests.instruction: The letter F is changed so that it looks like a backwards F. Which move did this?
quests.hint: Think about which move reverses left and right, like a mirror.
quests.explanation: A flip works like a mirror, so it changes F into a backwards F. A half turn would put the arms at the bottom instead, and a slide would not change the letter at all.
quests.funFact: Leonardo da Vinci wrote many of his notes in mirror writing.

quests.instruction: The letter L makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which description is correct?
quests.correctAnswer: A long bar across the top with a short leg going down on the left
options: A long bar across the bottom with a short leg going up on the right
A long bar across the top with a short leg going down on the left
A long bar down the left side with a short foot going left
quests.hint: Follow the corner of the L, then the long bar, then the short foot.
quests.explanation: The corner of the L moves from the bottom left to the top left. The long part, which pointed up, now points right, and the short foot, which pointed right, now points down.
quests.funFact: L-shaped brackets hold two boards together at a square corner.

quests.instruction: Which move leaves the letter H looking exactly the same?
options: A quarter turn followed by a flip
quests.hint: Picture H lying on its side after a quarter turn. Does it still look like an H?
quests.explanation: H looks the same upside down, so a half turn leaves it unchanged. After a quarter turn it lies on its side, and a flip does not stand it back up.
quests.funFact: H is one of the letters that looks the same after a half turn, along with I, N, O, S, X, and Z.

quests.instruction: A pointer faces east. It makes a quarter turn clockwise, and then a half turn counterclockwise. Which way does it face now?
quests.hint: Do each turn one at a time and write down the direction after each.
quests.explanation: A quarter turn clockwise from east points south. A half turn from south points north.
quests.funFact: A half turn changes any direction into its opposite, so south becomes north.

quests.instruction: A wide rectangle has a circle on its left end. It is flipped left to right and then makes a quarter turn counterclockwise. Where is the circle now?
quests.hint: Follow the circle through the flip first, then through the turn.
quests.explanation: The flip moves the circle from the left end to the right end. A quarter turn counterclockwise then carries the right end up to the top.
quests.funFact: Tracking one marked point through several moves is how game designers move characters on a screen.

quests.instruction: A number 6 is given a half turn. Which number does it look like?
quests.hint: Picture the loop at the bottom of the 6 moving to the top.
quests.explanation: A half turn moves the loop from the bottom to the top and the tail from the top to the bottom, which makes a 9.
quests.funFact: Because 6 and 9 turn into each other, house numbers like these often get an underline so people read them correctly.

quests.instruction: A worker wants to check whether a metal plate lying at an angle is a rectangle. Which measurements do not depend on how the plate is turned?
quests.correctAnswer: The lengths of its sides and the size of its corners
options: How high its top corner sits
The lengths of its sides and the size of its corners
quests.hint: Pick the facts that stay the same whichever way the plate is turned.
quests.explanation: Turning a plate does not change its side lengths or its corners. How high a corner sits and which side faces a direction both change when it is turned.
quests.funFact: Factories use these unchanging measurements to check that parts are the right shape however they are placed.

quests.instruction: A triangle with three equal sides is drawn pointing up, pointing down, and lying with a corner pointing sideways. How many different triangles are there?
quests.hint: Count different shapes, not different positions.
quests.explanation: All three drawings show the same triangle in different positions. Turning does not make a new triangle.
quests.funFact: A single triangle can be drawn in endlessly many positions on a page.

quests.instruction: Which description identifies a shape no matter how it is turned?
quests.correctAnswer: Four equal sides and four square corners
options: Four equal sides and four square corners
quests.hint: Choose a description that does not mention up, down, left, or right.
quests.explanation: Sides and corners stay the same under any turn, but words like top and left depend on how the shape is placed.
quests.funFact: Directions like left and right depend on where you stand, but a shape's sides and corners do not.

quests.instruction: The corners of a triangle are labeled A, B, and C in clockwise order. Its mirror image is drawn. Going clockwise around the mirror image, in what order do the letters appear?
quests.hint: A mirror reverses the direction you read around a shape.
quests.explanation: A mirror image reverses direction, so going clockwise around it reads the letters in the opposite order: A, C, B. The orders A, B, C and B, C, A are the same as the original.
quests.funFact: Left-handed scissors are made as mirror images of regular scissors.

quests.instruction: A triangle with three equal sides points up and has a dot on its top corner. It makes one third of a full turn clockwise. Where is the dot now?
quests.hint: A third of a turn moves each corner to the next corner around.
quests.explanation: A third of a turn clockwise moves the top corner to the bottom right corner, and the triangle looks the same as before except for the dot.
quests.funFact: Because the triangle looks the same after a third of a turn, only the dot shows that it moved.

quests.instruction: Which pair of shapes would not fit exactly on top of each other, even after turning and flipping?
quests.correctAnswer: Two squares with 5 cm and 6 cm sides
options: Two squares with 5 cm and 6 cm sides
Two triangles with sides of 3, 4, 5 cm and 5, 4, 3 cm
quests.hint: Turning and flipping cannot change side lengths.
quests.explanation: A 5 cm square and a 6 cm square have different side lengths, so no turn or flip can make them match. The other pairs have the same lengths.
quests.funFact: Cookie cutters make shapes that match exactly because each cutter has a fixed outline.
